# Model Evaluation Report — Isolation Forest baseline `iforest-20261031-s2026`

**Date:** 2026-10-31 · **Dataset:** Petosvahti synthetic Finnish stream — 2,000 customers, seed 2026, time-ordered splits 31 d warm-up / 21 d train / 7 d calibration / 14 d test; test = 106,198 tx, 463 fraud (0.4 %) · **Seed:** 2026 · **Artifact:** `models/fraud_model.joblib` (sha256 `ea54fb5d775e`)

*Generated by `petosvahti train --report`; every number below is reproducible from the seed. Model: `IsolationForest(n_estimators=300, max_samples=1024)` [R18][R19] on 12 per-customer features, isotonic calibration to P(fraud), policy approve < 20 ≤ review ≤ 85 < block.*

## Headline metrics

The test window is **replayed through the online `Scorer`** in time order — features, model, policy and the learning rule (blocked/reviewed payments never teach the profile) exactly as in production — so these are system metrics, not static-matrix metrics.

| Metric | Value | Target | Baseline comparison |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR-AUC | **0.943** | ≥ 0.70 (O1) | Supervised HistGradientBoosting (sees labels): 0.906 |
| ROC-AUC | 0.9933 | — | — |
| Recall @ review threshold (flagged = review + block) | **95.2 %** | | Static rules: 84.9 % |
| Precision @ review threshold | 88.2 % | | Static rules: 74.4 % |
| Recall @ block threshold | 81.6 % | | |
| Precision @ block threshold | 97.7 % | | |
| Legit payments blocked per 1 000 tx | 0.085 | | |
| Precision @ top-1 % | 43.1 % | | ceiling = fraud rate / 1 % = 43.6 % |
| Scoring latency p50 / p95 / p99 | 0.41 / 0.69 / 1.03 ms | p99 < 100 ms | scikit-learn `score_samples`: ~30 ms per row |

*Why PR-AUC and not accuracy [R20]: at 0.4 % fraud, predicting "all legit" scores 99.6 % accuracy and catches nothing.*

**Static rules baseline** = block if (≥ €1 000 to a new payee) or (≥ 5 attempts in an hour) or (new device from a new country) — the kind of rule set a bank starts with. It flags 5.0 per 1 000 tx.

**Business view:** of €419 146 attempted fraud in the test window, €328 100 was blocked outright and €90 483 held for review.

## Threshold analysis

Cut-offs are chosen on the **calibration window** (below, left) and only reported on test (right), so the test set never tunes the policy.

|---|---|---|---|

**Test window (replay)**

| Risk ≥ | Precision | Recall | Flagged per 1 000 tx |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 85.0 % | 95.7 % | 4.91 |

| 80 | 97.7 % | 81.6 % | 3.64 |
| 85 | 97.7 % | 81.6 % | 3.64 |
| 90 | 97.7 % | 81.6 % | 3.64 |
| 95 | 97.7 % | 81.6 % | 3.64 |

**Chosen:** review at risk ≥ 20, block above 85.

- *Review ≥ 20* — a human looks at anything with roughly a one-in-five chance of being fraud or worse. The review queue is 1.06 cases per 1 000 tx (≈ 11 per 10 000), which a small fraud desk can clear. This is the GDPR Art. 22 human-in-the-loop band [R9].
- *Block > 85* — automatic refusal only where precision stays ~97 %+; on instant rails (≤ 10 s, irrevocable [R1]) a block is the only intervention that works, so it must rarely hit a customer.
- The isotonic map is a step function, so neighbouring thresholds often give identical results (plateaus in the tables); moving a cut-off within a plateau changes nothing.

## Error analysis

**False negatives: 22** (Card testing: 21, APP scam (victim pays a mule): 1); median amount €3. Most common reason-code sets on missed fraud:

- `NEW_PAYEE + RAPID_SUCCESSION` — 11
- `NEW_DEVICE + NEW_PAYEE` — 8
- `NEW_COUNTRY + NEW_DEVICE + NEW_PAYEE` — 2
- `AMOUNT_UNUSUAL + INSTANT_HIGH_VALUE + NEW_PAYEE` — 1

- *Card testing*: the first one or two probes of a burst have no velocity yet and are €0.50–4 — indistinguishable from a coffee. Detection kicks in from the third attempt, which is when real card-testing defences trigger too.
- *APP scam*: the victim uses their own phone, at home, so the only signals are amount + new payee + instant rail. Isolation Forest splits on one feature at a time and isolates *combinations* poorly; the `instant_new_payee_log_amount` interaction feature and the 24 h beneficiary cooling-off recover most of it, the remainder are modest amounts for customers who often spend big.

**False positives: 59** (channels: mobilepay: 38, sepa_instant: 10, card: 8, online_bank: 2, siirto: 1). Reason-code sets:

- `NEW_PAYEE` — 21
- `NEW_PAYEE + NIGHT_TIME` — 9
- `HIGH_VELOCITY + NEW_PAYEE` — 5
- `HIGH_VELOCITY + NEW_PAYEE + RAPID_SUCCESSION` — 4
- `AMOUNT_UNUSUAL + INSTANT_HIGH_VALUE` — 3

These are genuine customer behaviour that looks like fraud — a burst of new second-hand purchases, a large payment to a brand-new payee at night. Most land in `review`, not `block`.

## Limitations & honesty section

- **Synthetic data, same author as the model.** The generator encodes my beliefs about Finnish fraud; the model is evaluated against those same beliefs. That is circular. These numbers show the pipeline works and the features carry signal; they do **not** predict performance on real bank traffic, where fraud adapts and labels are late, noisy and incomplete.
- **Kaggle benchmark not in this report.** The Kaggle credit-card set [R17] is PCA-anonymised card data with no customer, payee, device or rail — none of these features can be computed on it. `scripts/benchmark_kaggle.py` runs the same algorithm on it as a sanity check, separately.
- **Labels used twice:** for isotonic calibration and threshold choice, both on the calibration window, never on test. The forest itself is unsupervised.
- **Supervised reference is not tuned** and is trained on offline (learn-everything) features while being tested on online (approved-only) features; treat it as a rough upper bound, not a competitor.
- **Latency** is in-process, single-threaded, excluding HTTP and network; worst observed call 1132 ms (a GC or OS scheduling pause, not model compute). The API's `/metrics` reports end-to-end figures.
- **Concept drift is not modelled:** one stationary month of behaviour.

## Decision

Ship as the **baseline** for the scoring service and live demo. Next iteration: an autoencoder or a supervised challenger trained on analyst-confirmed `review` outcomes, compared on this same replay harness.
